Notes on conventions:
- All timestamps are in IST (UTC+5:30).
- Incident IDs follow the format INC-YYYY-NNN.
- Severity is classified as SEV1 (critical, customer-facing outage), SEV2 (major degradation or partial loss of function), SEV3 (minor impact, workaround available), SEV4 (cosmetic or non-user-facing).
- Status values: Closed, Resolved (awaiting verification), Monitoring, Open.
- Mean duration is measured from the incident open timestamp to the resolution timestamp (when the fix was confirmed and the incident was moved to Monitoring or Closed). It excludes time spent in post-resolution verification.
- Site percentage indicates the proportion of total incidents in 2024 that were reported from each site, based on the primary site of the reporting engineer. This is a legacy field retained for historical comparison; it is not used for capacity planning.

Service-Level Incident Summary (2024)

The Incident Management System export (S01) records Payments Gateway Service incident_count_2024 as 7 incidents. Record status: current. This count is current as of the export date and includes all incidents opened during the 2024 calendar year, regardless of whether they were subsequently closed or remain open. It does not include incidents that were opened in 2023 and carried over into 2024, nor does it include pre-empted alerts that were resolved without an incident record.

Site distribution percentages in the table above sum to 100.0% across all six services. The percentages are based on the primary site of the reporting engineer at the time the incident was opened. For incidents where the reporting engineer was not available at the time of opening (for example, an on-call engineer picked up a ticket that was originally filed by an automated monitor), the site is assigned based on the on-call rotation schedule for that day. This convention was changed in March 2024; prior to that, the site was assigned based on the site of the engineer who acknowledged the incident. The change was made to better reflect the origin of the report rather than the location of the responder. A comparison of the two conventions is available in the quarterly review for Q1 2024.

Mean duration is calculated using the resolution timestamp, which is the time at which the incident was marked as Resolved or Closed in IMS. For incidents that are still open at the time of this export, the duration is calculated as the time from opening to the export generation time (2025-01-05 14:22 IST), and these incidents are flagged in the per-incident table in Part 2. As of this export, all incidents listed in the table above have a status of Closed, with the exception of one incident in the Order Processing Service that remains in Monitoring status. The root causes for reopenings fell into two categories: incomplete fixes (INC-2024-004 and INC-2024-027) and configuration changes that were not validated in staging (INC-2024-027 and INC-2024-058). INC-2024-027 appears in both categories, as the initial fix addressed the immediate symptom but the underlying configuration issue was not identified until the second reopening.

# 16. Incident Detection Method

| Detection Method | Count | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| Automated Alerting | 33 | 80.5% |
| Customer Report | 5 | 12.2% |
| Manual Monitoring | 3 | 7.3% |
| **Total** | **41** | **100%** |
# 17. Incident Count by Service

The following table presents incident counts by service for calendar year 2024. Counts include new incidents and reopenings. A service is attributed as the affected service when the incident was opened; for incidents affecting multiple services, the primary affected service is used.

| Service | Incident Count |
|---|---|
| Payments Service | 11 |
| Order Processing Service | 9 |
| Customer Notification Service | 7 |
| Reporting and Analytics Service | 5 |
| Identity and Access Management | 4 |
| Inventory Service | 3 |
| Shipping Service | 2 |
| **Total** | **41** |

Incident counts are attributed to the data center hosting the primary instance of the affected service at the time of the incident. Failovers to the disaster recovery site are not reflected in site attribution.

| Site | Incident Count |
|---|---|
| Mumbai Data Center | 29 |
| Bengaluru Data Center | 12 |
| **Total** | **41** |

# 19. Incident Count by Severity

| Severity | Count | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | 6 | 14.6% |
| SEV2 | 15 | 36.6% |
| SEV3 | 20 | 48.8% |

# 21. Mean Time to Resolve by Severity

Mean time to resolve (MTTR) is calculated from incident open time to final closure time, including any reopening periods. MTTR is presented in hours.

| Severity | Mean Time to Resolve (hours) |
|---|---|
| SEV1 | 4.2 |
| SEV2 | 7.8 |
| SEV3 | 2.1 |

| Inventory Service | 3.1 |
| Shipping Service | 2.4 |

# 23. Top Incident Categories

Each incident is assigned one primary category at closure. Categories are reviewed quarterly; the category list was updated in Q3 2024 to split "Infrastructure" into "Compute" and "Network".

| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| Application Defect | 14 |
| Configuration Change | 9 |
| Dependency Outage | 7 |
| Capacity Exhaustion | 5 |
| Network | 4 |
| Compute | 2 |
| **Total** | **41** |

# 24. Incident Assignment and Handoff

The following table shows the number of times each incident was reassigned between teams before closure. Reassignment counts include initial assignment.

| Team | Assignments |
|---|---|
| Payments Team | 14 |
| Order Processing Team | 11 |
| Customer Notification Team | 9 |
| Platform Team | 8 |
| Data Engineering Team | 6 |
| Identity Team | 5 |

# 25. Open Incidents at Year End

No incidents were open as of 2024-12-31 23:59 IST. The last incident closure of the year was INC-2024-061, closed on 2024-12-28 16:45 IST.

# 26. Data Completeness Note

Incident records for 2024 are considered complete as of this export (2025-01-05). All incident records have a severity, affected service, open time, and closure time populated. No records are pending triage.

One data quality issue was identified during the year-end reconciliation: INC-2024-044 (Customer Notification Service) was initially recorded with an incorrect open time. The corrected open time is 2024-09-12 08:20 IST. The record was updated on 2024-09-13 and has been current since that date.

# 27. Comparison to 2023

For reference, the table below shows total incidents and MTTR for 2023. 2023 data was exported from the previous Incident Management System instance; incident IDs from 2023 are not directly comparable to 2024 IDs.

| Metric | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Total Incidents | 38 | 41 |
| SEV1 Incidents | 4 | 6 |
| SEV2 Incidents | 12 | 15 |
| SEV3 Incidents | 22 | 20 |
| MTTR (all incidents, hours) | 5.1 | 4.6 |

The increase in total incidents from 2023 to 2024 is within the expected range given the addition of the Inventory Service and Shipping Service to the production environment in February 2024. These two services together accounted for 5 incidents in 2024. Excluding those, incident count for the services present in both years was 36, a decrease of 2 from 2023.

The table below groups incidents by the hour (IST) at which they were opened. MTTR is calculated from open time to closure time, excluding time spent waiting for customer confirmation where that was recorded.

| Hour (IST) | Incidents | Avg MTTR (hours) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00:00–05:59 | 4 | 6.2 | Includes two overnight batch-related incidents |
| 06:00–11:59 | 9 | 4.1 | Morning peak, mostly SEV3 |
| 12:00–17:59 | 14 | 4.8 | Afternoon peak; includes INC-2024-044 |
| 18:00–23:59 | 14 | 4.3 | Evening incidents; one SEV1 at 21:15 |

No clear pattern of slower response during night hours was observed. The two SEV1 incidents opened between 00:00 and 05:59 were both related to the same upstream provider issue in March.

# 29. Incident Duration Distribution

Duration is measured from open to closure time in hours. Incidents shorter than 30 minutes are rounded to 0.5.

| Duration Range | Count | Share of Total |
|---|---|---|
| < 1 hour | 9 | 22% |
| 1–3 hours | 17 | 41% |
| 3–6 hours | 9 | 22% |
| 6–12 hours | 4 | 10% |
| > 12 hours | 2 | 5% |

# 30. Incidents by Day of Week

| Day | Incidents | SEV1 | SEV2 | SEV3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 7 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| Tuesday | 6 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Wednesday | 5 | 0 | 2 | 3 |
| Thursday | 8 | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| Friday | 7 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| Saturday | 5 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| Sunday | 3 | 0 | 1 | 2 |

Weekend incidents (Saturday and Sunday combined) totalled 8, with a lower share of SEV3 incidents compared to weekdays. This is consistent with reduced traffic and fewer code deployments on weekends.

# 31. Incident Origin and Initial Detection

Incidents are classified by how they were first detected. This field was populated for all incidents in 2024.

| Detection Method | Count |
|---|---|
| Automated alert | 29 |
| Customer report | 8 |
| Internal monitoring review | 3 |
| Scheduled test | 1 |

The customer-reported incidents were concentrated in the Payments Service (5) and Order Processing Service (2), with one for the Identity Service. Automated alerts were the primary detection method for all other services.

# 32. Recurrence of Incident Types

The table below lists incident types that occurred more than once in 2024, along with the month of each occurrence.

| Incident Type | Occurrences | Months |
|---|---|---|
| Database connection pool exhaustion | 4 | Feb, May, Aug, Nov |
| Upstream provider timeout | 3 | Mar, Jun, Sep |
| Certificate expiry | 2 | Apr, Oct |
| Memory leak | 2 | Jul, Dec |
| Configuration error | 2 | Jan, Aug |
| Disk full | 2 | Mar, Nov |

Database connection pool exhaustion occurred in four separate months, each time in a different service. The configuration errors in January and August were both traced to manual changes made outside the change management process; see Section 33.

# 33. Change-Related Incidents

Incidents are marked as change-related if a production change was approved and deployed within 24 hours before the incident open time, and the change was determined to be a contributing factor.

| Incident ID | Service | Date | Related Change | Outcome |

| INC-2024-011 | Identity | 2024-03-02 | CHG-2024-008 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-019 | Payments | 2024-04-18 | CHG-2024-011 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-027 | Platform | 2024-06-09 | CHG-2024-017 | Confirmed cause |

Six of the seven change-related incidents involved changes made by teams other than the service owner. The remaining incident (INC-2024-011) was caused by an Identity Team change. No change-related incidents occurred in the month of December.

Incident Management System Export – 2024 Summary (Part 1)

Source: Incident Management System (IMS)
Export generated on: 2025-01-05 14:22 IST
Reporting window: 2024-01-01 00:00 IST to 2024-12-31 23:59 IST
Export scope: All services tracked under IMS. This part covers the service-level aggregate table and site distribution notes. Part 2 will contain the per-incident timeline and assignment history.

Notes on conventions:
- All timestamps are in IST (UTC+5:30).
- Incident IDs follow the format INC-YYYY-NNN.
- Severity is classified as SEV1 (critical, customer-facing outage), SEV2 (major degradation or partial loss of function), SEV3 (minor impact, workaround available), SEV4 (cosmetic or non-user-facing).
- Status values: Closed, Resolved (awaiting verification), Monitoring, Open.
- Mean duration is measured from the incident open timestamp to the resolution timestamp (when the fix was confirmed and the incident was moved to Monitoring or Closed). It excludes time spent in post-resolution verification.
- Site percentage indicates the proportion of total incidents in 2024 that were reported from each site, based on the primary site of the reporting engineer. This is a legacy field retained for historical comparison; it is not used for capacity planning.

Service-Level Incident Summary (2024)

The Incident Management System export (S01) records Payments Gateway Service incident_count_2024 as 7 incidents. Record status: current. This count is current as of the export date and includes all incidents opened during the 2024 calendar year, regardless of whether they were subsequently closed or remain open. It does not include incidents that were opened in 2023 and carried over into 2024, nor does it include pre-empted alerts that were resolved without an incident record.

Site distribution percentages in the table above sum to 100.0% across all six services. The percentages are based on the primary site of the reporting engineer at the time the incident was opened. Incident records for 2024 are considered complete as of this export (2025-01-05). All incident records have a severity, affected service, open time, and closure time populated. No records are pending triage.

One data quality issue was identified during the year-end reconciliation: INC-2024-044 (Customer Notification Service) was initially recorded with an incorrect open time. The corrected open time is 2024-09-12 08:20 IST. The record was updated on 2024-09-13 and has been current since that date.

# 27. Comparison to 2023

For reference, the table below shows total incidents and MTTR for 2023. 2023 data was exported from the previous Incident Management System instance; incident IDs from 2023 are not directly comparable to 2024 IDs.

| Metric | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|
| Total Incidents | 38 | 41 |
| SEV1 Incidents | 4 | 6 |
| SEV2 Incidents | 12 | 15 |
| SEV3 Incidents | 22 | 20 |
| MTTR (all incidents, hours) | 5.1 | 4.6 |

The increase in total incidents from 2023 to 2024 is within the expected range given the addition of the Inventory Service and Shipping Service to the production environment in February 2024. These two services together accounted for 5 incidents in 2024. Excluding those, incident count for the services present in both years was 36, a decrease of 2 from 2023.

# 28. Incident Response Time by Time of Day

The table below groups incidents by the hour (IST) at which they were opened. MTTR is calculated from open time to closure time, excluding time spent waiting for customer confirmation where that was recorded.

| Hour (IST) | Incidents | Avg MTTR (hours) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00:00–05:59 | 4 | 6.2 | Includes two overnight batch-related incidents |
| 06:00–11:59 | 9 | 4.1 | Morning peak, mostly SEV3 |
| 12:00–17:59 | 14 | 4.8 | Afternoon peak; includes INC-2024-044 |
| 18:00–23:59 | 14 | 4.3 | Evening incidents; one SEV1 at 21:15 |

No clear pattern of slower response during night hours was observed. The two SEV1 incidents opened between 00:00 and 05:59 were both related to the same upstream provider issue in March.

# 29. Incident Duration Distribution

Duration is measured from open to closure time in hours. Incidents shorter than 30 minutes are rounded to 0.5.

| Duration Range | Count | Share of Total |
|---|---|---|
| < 1 hour | 9 | 22% |
| 1–3 hours | 17 | 41% |
| 3–6 hours | 9 | 22% |
| 6–12 hours | 4 | 10% |
| > 12 hours | 2 | 5% |

The two incidents longer than 12 hours were INC-2024-018 (Payments, 14.5 hours) and INC-2024-047 (Customer Notification Service, 13.2 hours). Both involved waiting on vendor patches.

# 30. Incidents by Day of Week

| Day | Incidents | SEV1 | SEV2 | SEV3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 7 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| Tuesday | 6 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Wednesday | 5 | 0 | 2 | 3 |
| Thursday | 8 | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| Friday | 7 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| Saturday | 5 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| Sunday | 3 | 0 | 1 | 2 |

Weekend incidents (Saturday and Sunday combined) totalled 8, with a lower share of SEV3 incidents compared to weekdays. This is consistent with reduced traffic and fewer code deployments on weekends.

# 31. Incident Origin and Initial Detection

Incidents are classified by how they were first detected. This field was populated for all incidents in 2024.

| Detection Method | Count |
|---|---|
| Automated alert | 29 |
| Customer report | 8 |
| Internal monitoring review | 3 |
| Scheduled test | 1 |

The customer-reported incidents were concentrated in the Payments Service (5) and Order Processing Service (2), with one for the Identity Service. Automated alerts were the primary detection method for all other services.

# 32. Recurrence of Incident Types

The table below lists incident types that occurred more than once in 2024, along with the month of each occurrence.

| Incident Type | Occurrences | Months |
|---|---|---|
| Database connection pool exhaustion | 4 | Feb, May, Aug, Nov |
| Upstream provider timeout | 3 | Mar, Jun, Sep |
| Certificate expiry | 2 | Apr, Oct |
| Memory leak | 2 | Jul, Dec |
| Configuration error | 2 | Jan, Aug |
| Disk full | 2 | Mar, Nov |

Database connection pool exhaustion occurred in four separate months, each time in a different service. The configuration errors in January and August were both traced to manual changes made outside the change management process; see Section 33.

# 33. Change-Related Incidents

Incidents are marked as change-related if a production change was approved and deployed within 24 hours before the incident open time, and the change was determined to be a contributing factor.

| Incident ID | Service | Date | Related Change | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| INC-2024-003 | Order Processing | 2024-01-14 | CHG-2024-002 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-011 | Identity | 2024-03-02 | CHG-2024-008 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-019 | Payments | 2024-04-18 | CHG-2024-011 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-027 | Platform | 2024-06-09 | CHG-2024-017 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-035 | Inventory | 2024-08-21 | CHG-2024-023 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-052 | Customer Notification | 2024-10-14 | CHG-2024-029 | Confirmed cause |
| INC-2024-058 | Shipping | 2024-11-30 | CHG-2024-034 | Confirmed cause |

Six of the seven change-related incidents involved changes made by teams other than the service owner. The remaining incident (INC-2024-011) was caused by an Identity Team change. No change-related incidents occurred in the month of December.
